memory_candidates.title: A shrinking headline count can hide growing work
memory_candidates.content: In the CSLib modal Tableau subsystem, an adversarial re-verification pass corrected a '77 local re-derivation sites' figure down to 55 exact-phrase occurrences — while simultaneously finding that every per-lemma spot-check was an UNDERCOUNT (modalSubfmls_trans 4x not 3x, modalKnownWorlds_fold_spec 6x not 4x, hasEdge_addEdge_cases 7x not 4x), that the per-file distribution omitted the largest file's 14 sites entirely, and that extraction must draw from two source files rather than one (hasEdge_addEdge_cases originates in Soundness.lean, not FmpMeasure.lean). When a headline metric is corrected downward, re-derive the scope from the component measurements rather than reading the smaller number as a scope reduction.

memory_candidates.title: A review-gate decision record is build-independent and can land on a red tree
memory_candidates.content: When a repository does not build for a reason outside the current task's territory, work whose entire evidence base is source-text measurement plus literature reading is still valid and should land rather than block. Record the build gate explicitly — including that every downstream acceptance gate reading 'checkInitImports clean' is vacuous until the owner clears it — and state that the record itself is build-independent. This keeps a red tree from stalling decision work while preventing anyone downstream from mistaking a command that fails for an unrelated reason for a passing gate.
